body.translated_text:
Now, the Thirty Verses on Consciousness-Only (<s>Triṃśikāvijñaptikārikā</s>).
This is the composition of the master <s>Vasubandhu</s>.

children.translated_text: The manifold figurative usage of 'self' and 'phenomena' (<s>dharma</s>) that occurs,
that [takes place] in the transformation of consciousness (<s>vijñāna-pariṇāma</s>); and that transformation is threefold. (Tvk 1)
Ripening (<s>vipāka</s>), that called 'thinking' (<s>manana</s>), and the cognition of objects —
Among these, the consciousness called 'storehouse' (<s>ālaya</s>) is the ripening, [and it is] the seed of everything (<s>sarva-bījaka</s>). (Tvk 2)
And it has [as its objects] imperceptible apprehensions, locations, and representations (<s>vijñapti</s>);
it is always accompanied by contact (<s>sparśa</s>), attention (<s>manaskāra</s>), feeling (<s>vit</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), and volition (<s>cetanā</s>). (Tvk 3)
Its feeling is equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>); and it is unobstructed and indeterminate (<s>anivṛta-avyākṛta</s>);
likewise contact and the rest. And it flows like the current of a river. (Tvk 4)
Its cessation [occurs] in the state of an <s>Arhat</s>. Dependent on it, there arises
the consciousness called 'mind' (<s>manas</s>), having thinking (<s>manana</s>) as its nature, with that [ālaya] as its support and object. (Tvk 5)
It is always accompanied by four afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), [which are] obstructed and indeterminate (<s>nivṛta-avyākṛta</s>):
those called self-view (<s>ātma-dṛṣṭi</s>), self-delusion (<s>ātma-moha</s>), self-conceit (<s>ātma-māna</s>), and self-love (<s>ātma-sneha</s>). (Tvk 6)
Wherever that [ālaya consciousness] is born, [the manas is accompanied] by other [mental factors] of that same nature, along with contact and the rest. But it does not exist in an <s>Arhat</s>,

children.text: na nirodhasamāpattau mārge lokottare na ca || 7 ||
children.translated_text: nor in the attainment of cessation (<s>nirodha-samāpatti</s>), nor on the supramundane path (<s>lokottara-mārga</s>). (Tvk 7)
This is the second transformation. The third is the sixfold
apprehension of objects; it is wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>), unwholesome (<s>akuśala</s>), or neither (<s>advaya</s>). (Tvk 8)
It is associated with universal [mental factors] (<s>sarvatraga</s>), with determined [factors] (<s>viniyata</s>), and with wholesome mental factors (<s>caitasa</s>);
likewise with afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) and secondary afflictions (<s>upakleśa</s>); and it has three kinds of feeling (<s>vedanā</s>). (Tvk 9)
The first [group, the universals, are]: contact (<s>sparśa</s>) and the rest, [namely] desire (<s>chanda</s>), resolve (<s>adhimokṣa</s>), and memory (<s>smṛti</s>), along with
concentration (<s>samādhi</s>) and understanding (<s>dhī</s>). The determined [factors are]: faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), then shame (<s>hrī</s>), and modesty (<s>apatrapā</s>), (Tvk 10)
non-attachment (<s>alobha</s>) and the [other] two [of the triad], vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>), together with diligence (<s>apramāda</s>),
and non-harming (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) — these are the wholesome ones. The afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) are: desire (<s>rāga</s>), aversion (<s>pratigha</s>), and delusion (<s>mūḍha</s>), (Tvk 11)
conceit (<s>māna</s>), [wrong] view (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>), and doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>). And then anger (<s>krodha</s>) and resentment (<s>upanāha</s>),

children.text: mrakṣaḥ pradāśa īrṣyārtha mātsaryaṃ saha māyayā || 12 ||
children.translated_text: concealment (<s>mrakṣa</s>), malice (<s>pradāśa</s>), envy (<s>īrṣyā</s>), selfishness (<s>mātsarya</s>), together with deceit (<s>māyā</s>), (Tvk 12)

dissimulation (<s>śāṭhya</s>), arrogance (<s>mada</s>), harmfulness (<s>vihiṃsā</s>), shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>), lack of modesty (<s>anapatrapā</s>), torpor (<s>styāna</s>), restlessness (<s>uddhava</s>),
faithlessness (<s>āśraddha</s>), then laziness (<s>kausīdya</s>), heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>), and forgetfulness (<s>muṣitā smṛti</s>), (Tvk 13)
distraction (<s>vikṣepa</s>), and non-awareness (<s>asamprajanya</s>), remorse (<s>kaukṛtya</s>), and drowsiness (<s>middha</s>) as well,
and initial thought (<s>vitarka</s>) and sustained thought (<s>vicāra</s>) — these are the secondary afflictions, [the last four being] of two kinds in two [categories]. (Tvk 14)
Of the five [sense] consciousnesses, their arising in the root consciousness [occurs] according to conditions,

children.text: vijñānānāṃ saha na vā taraṅgāṇāṃ yathā jale || 15 ||
children.translated_text: together or not, like waves in water. (Tvk 15)
The arising of mind-consciousness (<s>mano-vijñāna</s>) [occurs] at all times, except in the unconscious state (<s>asaṃjñika</s>),
the two attainments [of cessation and unconsciousness], dreamless sleep (<s>middha</s>), and fainting (<s>mūrchanā</s>), and [other] mindless [states]. (Tvk 16)
This transformation of consciousness is conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>); what is conceptualized [by it]
does not exist as such. Therefore, all this is mere representation (<s>vijñaptimātra</s>). (Tvk 17)
For consciousness, which contains all seeds, transforms in such and such ways,

children.text: yātyanyonyavaśād yena vikalpaḥ sa sa jāyate || 18 ||
children.translated_text: proceeding through mutual influence; from that, such and such conceptualization arises. (Tvk 18)
The latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of actions (<s>karman</s>), together with the latent impressions of the twofold grasping (<s>grāha-dvaya</s>),
when the previous ripening is exhausted, they produce another ripening. (Tvk 19)

children.text: yena yena vikalpena yadyad vastu vikalpyate /
children.translated_text: By whatever conceptualization whatever object is conceptualized,

children.text: parikalpita evāsau svabhāvo na sa vidyate || 20 ||
children.translated_text: that [nature] is the imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>) nature itself — it does not [truly] exist. (Tvk 20)
The dependent nature (<s>paratantra-svabhāva</s>), however, is conceptualization arisen from conditions;

children.text: niṣpannastasya pūrveṇa sadā rahitatā tu yā || 21 ||
children.translated_text: the perfected (<s>niṣpanna</s>) [nature] is the perpetual absence of the former [imagined nature] in the latter [dependent nature]. (Tvk 21)

children.text: ata eva sa naivānyo nānanyaḥ paratantrataḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it [the perfected nature] is neither identical with nor different from the dependent [nature];
it should be described like impermanence and the like — when the one is not seen, the other is not seen [either]. (Tvk 22)
With reference to the three kinds of own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), the threefold absence of own-nature (<s>niḥsvabhāvatā</s>)
of all phenomena (<s>dharma</s>) has been taught — [that is,] the naturelessness [of all things]. (Tvk 23)
The first [the imagined] is without own-nature by virtue of its very definition; the second, however,
does not exist by itself — that is the other [kind of] naturelessness. (Tvk 24)
And the ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>) of all phenomena (<s>dharma</s>) is that; because it is also suchness (<s>tathatā</s>),
being ever thus in nature, it is itself consciousness-only (<s>vijñaptimātratā</s>). (Tvk 25)
As long as consciousness does not abide in consciousness-only,
the latent tendency (<s>anuśaya</s>) of the twofold grasping does not cease. (Tvk 26)
Even [thinking] 'this is mere representation only,' if one apprehends
something placed before [oneself], one does not abide in that 'mere' [consciousness-only]. (Tvk 27)
When consciousness no longer apprehends any object (<s>ālambana</s>),
then it is established in consciousness-only, because in the absence of what is grasped, there is no grasping of it. (Tvk 28)
It is without mind (<s>acitta</s>), without apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>); and that is supramundane knowledge (<s>lokottara-jñāna</s>).
The transformation of the basis (<s>āśraya-parāvṛtti</s>) is twofold, through the elimination of defilement (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>). // Tvk 29 //
That very [basis] is the uncontaminated element (<s>anāsrava-dhātu</s>), inconceivable, wholesome, and permanent;
It is blissful, the liberation-body (<s>vimuktikāya</s>); it is called <s>Dharma</s> — this [is the attainment] of the Great Sage (<s>Mahāmuni</s>). // Tvk 30 //

body.translated_text: The <s>Triṃśikāvijñaptikārikāḥ</s> (Thirty Verses on Consciousness-Only) are concluded.
This is the composition of the teacher <s>Vasubandhu</s>.
